findings.current: The heavily built old man landed on the Thousand-Year Spider, using its enormous, barely living, convulsing body as a cushion.
findings.defect: The source says he lands on the ground with the spider’s body serving as a cushion. The current sentence instead says he lands on the spider. It also drops the source’s explicit contrast that “enormous” describes the spider better than “large.”
findings.rationale: The Korean says 지면에 내려앉은 (“landed on the ground”) and contrasts 크다 with 거대하다 to emphasize the spider’s scale.
findings.replacement: The heavily built old man landed on the ground, using the Thousand-Year Spider—better described as enormous than large—as a cushion while it convulsed, barely alive.

summary: One physical-detail error remains: the Beast Miao King lands on the ground, cushioned by the spider, not on the spider itself.
